subject: Literature
title: Zora Neale Hurston's Their Eyes Were Watching God
description: A quick, practical guide to Zora Neale Hurston's Their Eyes Were Watching God.

hook.text: Zora Neale Hurston wrote a masterpiece that was forgotten for decades until Alice Walker literally found her unmarked grave.

buildup.text: Their Eyes Were Watching God follows Janie Crawford's journey through three marriages toward self-discovery and freedom.

discovery.text: Hurston wrote in the vernacular of Black Southern speech, preserving voices that literary fiction had ignored.

twist.text: Richard Wright attacked the novel for not being political enough, and it fell out of print for thirty years.

climax.text: Hurston proved that Black women's interior lives were worthy of literary attention and lyrical beauty.

punchline.text: A lost masterpiece waited thirty years for someone to listen.

quiz.question: How was Hurston's Their Eyes Were Watching God rediscovered?
options: A university professor found it in a used bookshop
Alice Walker searched for Hurston's unmarked grave and championed her work
A Hollywood studio adapted it into a film
